work_item.title: Dark/Light Theme Implementation
work_item.description: 🚩 AC Addressed (Required) Introduce light/dark theme selection entirely within the existing Python-rendered web UI. Ensure query syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible under both themes. Persist the user’s theme choice across requests using local storage. 💡 What do you want to accomplish? (Required) Improve user experience by allow users to toggle between dark/light themes. 📋 Testability Considerations (Required) Unit tests to check the new dark/light theme functionality.
acceptance_criteria: User can toggle between dark and light themes from the UI
Syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible in both themes
User's theme choice persists across page reloads and requests via local storage
Unit tests verify theme switching and persistence functionality

analysis.summary: Implement a dark/light theme toggle in the Python-rendered web UI, ensuring syntax highlighting and result panels are legible in both modes, and persist user selection via local storage.
technical_requirements: Add theme toggle UI element to the Python-rendered web interface
Apply CSS for both dark and light themes, including syntax highlighting and result panel styles
Persist user theme selection using browser local storage
Ensure theme selection is applied on every page load/request
Unit tests for theme switching logic and persistence
acceptance_criteria: User can toggle between dark and light themes from the UI
Syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible in both themes
User's theme choice persists across page reloads and requests via local storage
Unit tests verify theme switching and persistence functionality
risks: Ensuring all UI elements (including syntax highlighting and result panels) are styled correctly for both themes
Potential issues with theme persistence across different browsers or devices
No frontend framework; may require manual DOM manipulation and CSS management
Testing UI changes in Python-rendered templates without a JS framework
analysis.recommended_approach: Define CSS classes for dark and light themes, including specific rules for syntax highlighting and result panels. Add a theme toggle button to the UI, and use JavaScript to switch themes and store the selection in local storage. On page load, read the stored theme and apply it. Write unit tests for the theme toggle logic and persistence. Ensure Python templates render the toggle and apply the correct theme class.

implementation_steps.description: Add theme CSS styles and update styles.py to include them

instructions: Define CSS variables for light theme at the top of the CSS string: --bg-color: #f8f9fa; --text-color: #333; --primary-color: #0066cc; --panel-bg: #fff; --panel-border: #ddd; --syntax-bg: #f4f4f4; --syntax-keyword: #0066cc; --syntax-string: #22863a; --syntax-comment: #6a737d.

Define CSS variables for dark theme inside a .dark-theme class: --bg-color: #1a1a1a; --text-color: #e0e0e0; --primary-color: #4da6ff; --panel-bg: #222; --panel-border: #444; --syntax-bg: #23272e; --syntax-keyword: #4da6ff; --syntax-string: #7ec699; --syntax-comment: #999.

Refactor all existing CSS rules to use these variables, e.g., body { background: var(--bg-color); color: var(--text-color); }, .result-panel { background: var(--panel-bg); border-color: var(--panel-border); }, etc.
Update syntax highlighting CSS selectors to use theme variables for background and text colors, ensuring legibility in both themes.
Add .theme-toggle-btn styles for the toggle button (padding, border-radius, background, hover effect) using CSS variables.

implementation_steps.validation: presentation/styles.py contains CSS variables for both themes, .dark-theme class, and all major UI elements and syntax highlighting use these variables.

implementation_steps.description: Add theme toggle UI button and wire JavaScript to HTML template

instructions: In the HTML template string, add a <button id='theme-toggle' class='theme-toggle-btn'>🌙 Dark Mode</button> to the header or navigation section.

Before the closing </body> tag, insert an inline <script> block that: (1) checks localStorage for 'theme', (2) applies 'dark-theme' class to <body> if theme is 'dark', (3) sets the button text to 🌙 Dark Mode or ☀️ Light Mode accordingly, (4) adds a click event listener to #theme-toggle that toggles the theme, updates localStorage, and updates the button text.
Ensure the script runs on every page load and applies the correct theme before rendering content.
Reference the .theme-toggle-btn CSS class for styling (from styles.py) in the template's <style> section if not already present.

implementation_steps.validation: presentation/html_template.py renders the toggle button, includes working JavaScript for theme switching and persistence, and applies the correct theme class on page load.

implementation_steps.description: Ensure result panels and syntax highlighting remain legible in both themes

instructions: Review all result panel and syntax highlighting HTML elements to ensure they use classes/selectors that are styled in styles.py with theme variables.
If any inline styles or hardcoded colors exist for result panels or syntax highlighting, refactor them to use CSS classes and theme variables instead.
Test rendering with both themes to confirm legibility.

implementation_steps.validation: Result panels and syntax highlighting are styled via theme variables and are legible in both dark and light modes.

implementation_steps.description: Add unit tests for theme switching and persistence logic

instructions: Create tests that simulate theme switching by mocking localStorage and DOM manipulation.
Test that the correct theme class is applied to <body> based on localStorage value.
Test that clicking the toggle button updates localStorage and the theme class.
Test that syntax highlighting and result panel elements have the correct computed styles in both themes.
Use Python's unittest or pytest framework, and mock JS/DOM interactions as needed.

implementation_steps.validation: Unit tests cover theme switching, persistence, and UI element legibility.

implementation.pr_description: Implemented dark/light theme toggle feature with CSS variables, UI button, JavaScript logic for localStorage persistence, and unit tests for theme switching and legibility.
